newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy govt wins Albanian refugee confidence test.
newsitem.headline: Italy govt wins Albanian refugee confidence test.

text.p: The Italian government won a confidence vote in the lower house of parliament on Thursday to push into law a cabinet decree on measures covering Albanian refugees entering the country.

The measures had been threatened by hundreds of blocking amendments introduced by the separatist Northern League party. It was the 22nd confidence vote Prime Minister Romano Prodi's coalition has called and won since taking office a year ago.
Thursday's do-or-die motion was carried by 306 votes to 192, a parliamentary official said. The decree has already been approved by the upper house of parliament.

The cabinet introduced the decree in March after thousands of refugees flooded into Italy to escape turmoil in nearby Albania. The draft law gives the Albanians 90 days stay-of-leave in Italy after which they have to return home.

Under a constitutional court ruling, cabinet decrees must be converted into law within 60 days or lapse. That deadline is on Monday and the government said the confidence vote was necessary to sidestep the League amendments.
Prodi's centre-left coalition won the confidence vote thanks to the support of the hard-left Communist Refoundation, which is not in the government but guarantees its majority in the lower house.
